verses.1: In the ninth year of his reign, in the twelfth month, on the twentieth day of that month, came Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. All his army also arrived at Jerusalem. They built walls around the city.
verses.2: And the city entered the citadel after twelve years of King Zadokiah’s reign.
verses.3: On the ninth day of the month, the hunger in the city became worse. There was no bread for the people of that land.
verses.4: And the city and all the soldiers died that night through the gates, between the walls of the king’s garden. And the enemies surrounded the city. They went along the streets of the city.
verses.5: And the army of murderers pursued the king. They caught him in the middle of the night. All of his army was destroyed.
verses.6: And they brought the king to King Babylon, Rebelatha. They spoke with him about the judgment that would be given.
verses.7: And he slaughtered the sons of Zadkiya before his eyes. He also blinded Zadkiya’s eyes. They were destroyed by their own actions, and they were brought to death.
verses.8: And in the fifth month, on the seventeenth day of the month, it was the year 85 years after King Nebuchadnezzar became king of Babylon. Nebuzaradan, a high-ranking servant of King Babylon, ruled in Jerusalem.
verses.9: And he destroyed the Temple of God, as well as the king’s palace. He also burned down all the houses in Jerusalem, and every large building there.
verses.10: And all the armies around Jerusalem were destroyed by those fierce warriors.
verses.11: And all the people who remained in the city, and those who fell upon King Babylon. And Nebuzaradan, the chief officer, also brought them forth.
verses.12: And from the land’s surface, many treasures were left for those who cultivate and work the land.
verses.13: And the pillars of the temple of Nebuchadnezzar, and the windows and the sea of Nebuchadnezzar, which were in the temple of God, were broken down by the enemies. They carried away their treasures into the sea.
verses.14: And all those tools and instruments that are used for cutting and shaping things, as well as all those devices used for measuring and weighing.
verses.15: And the bracelets and necklaces that were made of gold, and those made of silver. They were bought by many wealthy people.
verses.16: The two pillars of the temple, and all the other structures that Solomon built for the House of God, were not worth anything compared to all these other things.
verses.17: It’s twelve amas from where the first idol stood. There’s a seal on it. The seal is three amas in length. There are also ropes around the seal. All around, there’s ropes everywhere. And the same applies to the second idol, which is also covered with ropes.
verses.18: And Raab-Tabach took Seraya, the chief priest, and Tzfanya, the deputy priest. He also took the three men who were responsible for guarding the doors.
verses.19: And from the city, he took one officer who was in charge of the soldiers. He also took five men who could recognize the king’s face. These men were found in the city. And there was also the commander of the army, who led the people of that land. There were sixty men from the people of that land who were found in the city.
verses.20: And Nebuzaradan, the chief officer, took them and sent them to king Babylon, Rezabatha.
verses.21: And the king of Babylon captured them and killed them at Babylon itself, in the land of Hamat. Thus, the Jews were destroyed from their land.
verses.22: And the people who remained in the land of Judah, to whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had left Gideon as ruler over them.
verses.23: And all the soldiers and men heard this. It seemed as though King Babylon had placed Gedaliah in charge. They went to Gedaliah’s house. There, Elisha son of Shunash, Jonathan son of Eqtesai, and Shemaiah son of Netanah, along with their followers, listened to what was said.
verses.24: And Gedaliah and his people sat with them. He said to them, “Do not fear those who dwell in the land, those who serve the king of Babylon. May God be with you.”
verses.25: On the seventh day of the month, Ismael son of Nethaniah son of Eliashar, from the family of the kings, came with ten men. They attacked David and killed him. They also killed all the Jews and the priests who were with him at the temple.
verses.26: And all the people, from the youngest to the oldest, along with the officers of the army, came out of Egypt, because they feared the Pharaoh’s soldiers.
verses.27: In the thirty-seventh year of the reign of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Elisha, king of Babylon, carried off the head of Jehoiachin from the house of Kelaya.
verses.28: And Thoboth spoke to him, and he placed his throne above the throne of the kings who were in Babylon.
verses.29: And he hated the food of gold and silver. He always ate bread before him, every day of his life.
verses.30: And a constant punishment was given to him by the king, every day of his life.
